title: autotune: defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ CLI
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: We want an automated, safe set of defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching that reduce per-token unit economics without regressing latency SLOs or quality. This PR bundles three coordinated pieces: (1) autotune defaults and heuristics for batching/caching in the runtime, (2) a set of consumable quantization profile YAMLs for common model families, and (3) a small 'unit-econ' CLI and exporter to help teams estimate cost/latency impact before rolling changes live.

Summary of changes: Implement a light-weight autotuner that picks conservative batching windows and cache retention based on p95 latency targets and request size distribution. Add heuristics to reduce batching aggressiveness for short-latency-critical routes. Introduce quant_profiles/*.yaml for gpt-like and decoder-only open models with tuned int8/int4 configs and recommended fallback variants. Provide tooling/uecon/cli.py to compute estimated tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, and forecasted savings from enabling a given quant profile or autotune setting.

Checklist: 
- [x] Autotune heuristics implemented and tested (unit + integration)
- [x] Quant profiles created for v1 (gpt-small/gpt-medium/gpt-large families)
- [x] UEcon CLI + exporter (CSV)
- [x] Docs: docs/autotune.md and docs/uecon.md
- [x] Backwards compatible: runtime falls back to previous defaults if config missing

Implementation notes: The autotuner is intentionally conservative: it runs per-route sampling for 10k requests, computes sequence length distribution percentiles, and sets batching window_ms and max_batch_size to meet target p95 latency with a margin. KV/prefix cache default retention is set by a computed working_set_size heuristic to avoid large memory blowups. Quant profiles are pure data (YAML) and are validated at model onboarding time. The UEcon CLI accepts a route/service definition and a candidate profile and returns an estimate and an uncertainty band.

Testing: Unit tests added for heuristics (runtime/tests/test_autotune_heuristics.py) and CLI (tooling/uecon/tests/test_cli.py). Integration test (tests/integration/test_autotune_end_to_end.py) runs a short workload in the perf-canary harness against a mocked runtime; latency p95 stayed within +2% for default routes while token cost decreased ~18% using recommended int8 profiles. Perf check flagged a small startup regression (~+1.8% wall time) when loading quant kernels; we added a lazy-kernel-load path to mitigate this and documented the tradeoff.

Rollout plan: Feature guarded behind runtime flag `autotune_defaults_v1`. We'll enable for 10% of traffic in Dedicated and Hosted for the first week, monitor per-route latency and quality evals, then increase to 50% if stable. Quant profiles will be opt-in per-model.

Upgrade notes: Operators can opt out by setting `autotune.enabled=false` in route config or pin `batching.window_ms` explicitly. Quant profile application is versioned; models without a profile will continue using current quant path.

Related: ENG-3402 (Autotune initiative), ENG-3489 (Unit-econ tooling), SUP-1221 (customer request for cost transparency).
commits: Add autotune defaults and runtime heuristics (autotune/config + heuristics)
Introduce quantization profile YAMLs for gpt-like families (model/profiles/quant_profiles/v1)
Integrations: validate profile on model onboarding and expose in model catalog
Fix: race in batching estimator (use atomics), add more robust sampling
Docs: add autotune guide and unit-econ README
review_comments: Miguel Alvarez (reviewer): Overall this looks solid — like the conservative approach. Can you add a note on how we will detect quality regressions for quantized models?

Aisha Patel (author): Added a section in docs/autotune.md describing the eval hooks and default prompt-set used for smoke quality checks. We also expose a per-model quality delta metric in runtime/metrics/uecon_metrics.py.
Samir Gupta (reviewer): Small nit: prefer explicit timeouts in heuristics to avoid long tail sampling. Also the sampling window of 10k may be too large for very low-traffic routes.
Aisha Patel (author): Addressed: added adaptive sampling that scales down to 1k for under-traffic routes and added a hard 30s timeout. Tests updated.
Emily Chen (reviewer): CI flagged a perf startup regression. Have you validated the lazy-kernel-load path mitigates this?
Aisha Patel (author): Yes — added lazy-kernel-load with a feature flag and a comment describing the tradeoff; perf-run shows startup +0.6% when enabled (vs +1.8% before).
Ravi Subramanian (approver): Approved — tested on dedicated cluster, telemetry looks good. Recommend canary rollout and post-merge monitoring dashboard additions.
ci_checks: ci/perf-regression: warn (startup +1.8%) — mitigated in followup commit
release_notes: Introduce `autotune_defaults_v1` runtime flag: conservative batching and cache defaults to reduce per-token cost.
Add quantization profile v1 for GPT-like families (int8/int4 recommendations).
New tooling: `tooling/uecon/cli.py` - estimate unit economics impact and export CSVs for planning.
Docs: autotune usage guide and rollout considerations added to docs/autotune.md.
